scenario.name: CrowdStrike, Kaspersky & Mandiant — Lazarus (SmoothOperator): 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain & Gopuram
scenario.shortSubtitle: CrowdStrike · Kaspersky GReAT · Mandiant · Trojanized ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll & ICONICSTEALER
scenario.overview: Think of a bright neighborhood supermarket filled with stocked grocery aisles, rolling shopping carts, barcode price stickers, and busy checkout conveyor belts. Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the barcode price scanner blending in with everyday guests, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the checkout cashier's station. When the store manager reconciles the checkout receipt tape against the aisle inventory count and overhead camera, the swapped barcode trick is caught red-handed. In this scenario (CVE-2023-29059, CrowdStrike, Kaspersky & Mandiant, Lazarus (SmoothOperator): 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain & Gopuram) at 10.10.24, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sideloading Trojanized ffmpeg.dll, then fetching icon1.ico..icon14.ico from GitHub, then executing In-Memory ICONICSTEALER. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Sideloading Trojanized ffmpeg.dll, then Fetching icon1.ico..icon14.ico from GitHub, then Executing In-Memory ICONICSTEALER, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 7 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: TROJANIZED FFMPEG.DLL SIDE-LOADING & 0xFEEDFACE RC4 DECRYPTION
stages.subtitle: Signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe loads trojanized ffmpeg.dll and decrypts d3dcompiler_47.dll
stages.description: Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the barcode price scanner blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the checkout cashier go about their routine. When an employee launches the legitimately signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe softphone client, Windows loads the co-located library ffmpeg.dll (which was trojanized inside 3CX’s build pipeline, CVE-2023-29059). Inside ffmpeg.dll, a malicious initialization thread creates the event AVMonitorEvent, opens the neighboring file d3dcompiler_47.dll (a legitimate-looking Direct3D shader library whose valid digital signature was stripped so an encrypted payload could be appended after the 4-byte magic marker 0xFEEDFACE), and decrypts that payload directly into RWX memory using the RC4 stream cipher with hardcoded key "3jB(2bsG#@c7". Why split the malware across three files (3CXDesktopApp.exe + ffmpeg.dll + d3dcompiler_47.dll)? Because 3CXDesktopApp.exe keeps its valid 3CX digital signature, ffmpeg.dll contains only a tiny RC4 reader with no C2 URLs, and the encrypted shellcode sits inert inside d3dcompiler_47.dll. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ TROJANIZED FFMPEG.DLL / ⇠#1 ACK RC4 Key 3jB(2bsG#@c7) from Node ① (#1 3CX Update & GitHub Dead-Drop) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike / Kaspersky EDR SIEM).
stages.mitreTechniqueName: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain

stages.title: GITHUB ICON1.ICO DEAD-DROP RESOLVER & AES-GCM C2 EXTRACTION
stages.subtitle: Fetching raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon*.ico to resolve C2
stages.description: At the checkout lane, the cashier slides the box across the glowing barcode scanner, which blindly trusts the swapped sticker instead of inspecting what is inside the box. Here in Step 2 inside the supermarket, the intruder approaches the barcode price scanner disguised as a regular visitor without disturbing the locked stockroom back door. Once decrypted in memory, the stage-2 shellcode uses a Dead Drop Resolver (MITRE T1102.001, connecting to a trusted public service like GitHub so corporate firewalls allow the traffic) by sending an HTTPS GET request to raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon1.ico (through icon14.ico). At the very end of the valid icon image sits an appended Base64 string prefixed with "$" (which the malware extracts and decrypts using AES-GCM to reveal the real command-and-control URL, such as https://akamaicontainer.com/gl or https://msstorageboxes.com/eb). Even after GitHub took down the IconStorages repository, the shellcode also contained a fallback list of hardcoded C2 domains disguised to look like Akamai, Azure, and Microsoft storage services. In the documented Sysmon EID 22 (DNS) / HTTPS exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Enterprise Workstation (3CX), Enterprise Workstation (3CX) responds with ACK AES-GCM C2 URL (confirming that the GITHUB .ICO DEAD-DROP request succeeded on Enterprise Workstation (3CX) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 IN-MEMORY ICONICSTEALER & KASPERSKY GOPURAM BACKDOOR DEPLOYMENT). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ GITHUB .ICO DEAD-DROP / ⇠#2 ACK AES-GCM C2 URL) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Enterprise Workstation (3CX)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike / Kaspersky EDR SIEM).

keySpecs.value: Appended Base64 string starting with "$" at EOF of .ico

stages.title: IN-MEMORY ICONICSTEALER & KASPERSKY GOPURAM BACKDOOR DEPLOYMENT
stages.subtitle: Harvesting browser credentials and deploying Gopuram on high-value targets
stages.description: The checkout register rings up the disguised item as a harmless penny snack and prints an official supermarket receipt, letting the cart roll right out the automatic glass doors. In this final step inside the supermarket, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the checkout cashier's station until the receipt tape & aisle camera catches the mismatch. Connecting to the decrypted C2 URL with an encrypted "tutma=" cookie, the loader downloads and reflectively loads a third-stage DLL strictly in memory: ICONICSTEALER (an information stealer documented by Mandiant and CrowdStrike that enumerates the workstation and reads SQLite History and Login Data files from Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Mozilla Firefox). Furthermore, as Kaspersky GReAT uncovered, on high-value cryptocurrency and financial victims the threat actor deployed Gopuram (a sophisticated modular C2 backdoor used exclusively by the Lazarus group). Mandiant subsequently traced how the 3CX supply chain attack itself began: Lazarus had earlier trojanized the website installer for Trading Technologies’ X_TRADER software, which an employee at 3CX downloaded, creating a supply-chain-to-supply-chain cascade. In the documented EDR Memory / File Access exchange from Enterprise Workstation (3CX) to ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll, ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll responds with ACK In-Memory DLL (confirming that the ICONICSTEALER & GOPURAM request succeeded on ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll and completing the final execution objective of CrowdStrike, Kaspersky & Mandiant, Lazarus (SmoothOperator): 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain & Gopuram). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ ICONICSTEALER & GOPURAM / ⇠#3 ACK In-Memory DLL) from Node ③ (#3 Enterprise Workstation (3CX)) to Node ④ (#4 ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike / Kaspersky EDR SIEM).

detectionRule.title: CrowdStrike / Kaspersky YARA — 3CX Trojanized ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule Lazarus_3CX_SupplyChain_d3dcompiler_Payload {
  meta:
    author = "CrowdStrike / Kaspersky GReAT / Mandiant"
    cve = "CVE-2023-29059"
  strings:
    $marker = { FE ED FA CE }
    $rc4_key = "3jB(2bsG#@c7" ascii
    $mutex = "AVMonitorEvent" wide ascii
  condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5a4d and 2 of them
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Uninstall compromised 3CXDesktopApp versions (18.12.407 and 18.12.416) immediately and update to clean builds signed with the rotated 3CX certificate.

detectionRule.title: 3CXDesktopApp Connecting to Lazarus C2 or GitHub IconStorages Dead-Drop
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain Malicious Network Beacon (CVE-2023-29059)
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\3CXDesktopApp.exe'
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'akamaicontainer.com'
      - 'azureonlinestorage.com'
      - 'msstorageboxes.com'
      - 'githubusercontent.com'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Block all known SmoothOperator C2 domains at the DNS/proxy layer and hunt for 3CXDesktopApp.exe initiating connections to non-PBX external domains.
